title: Merge Two Sorted Linked Lists
summary: Splice two ordered linked chains into one sorted chain.
statement: You are given the heads of two singly linked lists whose values are sorted in nondecreasing order. Merge them by reconnecting the existing nodes, then return the head of the combined sorted list. The interface displays linked lists as arrays, but your function receives `ListNode` objects.
constraints: Each input list is sorted in nondecreasing order.
Reuse the supplied nodes rather than allocating a separate node for every value.
brute_force_solution:
def merge_sorted_linked_lists(list1, list2):
    values = []
    while list1:
        values.append(list1.val)
        list1 = list1.next
    while list2:
        values.append(list2.val)
        list2 = list2.next
    dummy = ListNode()
    tail = dummy
    for value in sorted(values):
        tail.next = ListNode(value)
        tail = tail.next
    return dummy.next
hints: At every step, the smaller current node must come next in the merged chain.
Use a temporary dummy head so attaching the first real node needs no special case.
Move a tail pointer forward after linking the smaller of `list1` and `list2`, then attach the nonempty remainder.
A dummy head and two moving list pointers merge the chains in linear time and constant auxiliary space.
editorial: Create a temporary dummy head and keep a tail at the end of the merged portion. Compare the two current node values, connect the tail to the smaller node, and advance only that input. Once either input ends, connect the remaining chain directly because it is already sorted. Return `dummy.next`; only the temporary sentinel is new, while all result nodes come from the inputs.

tests.explanation: Taking the smaller current node from each chain produces [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4] without sorting again.
When the first chain is empty, the existing second chain is already the complete merged result.
